_readme: Comfy Cloud workflows DWARP can run. One entry per graph; the graph itself is a ComfyUI workflow
saved in API format (Workflow -> Export (API)) sitting next to this file.
An entry says where DWARP's own values go, by node id and input name, so the engine never has to
know what the graph is made of:
graph   the API-format file in this folder
short   one word for run labels, as in "h3 · render"
saver   the node whose output IS the render. Read outputs from this one only: a LoadVideo node
reports the file it read in the same shape as a real output and would otherwise win.
prompt  [node, input] the text goes on

prompt_hint {"weak": true, "note": "...", "dead_on_fast": true} — for a graph whose text
          encoder barely moves the picture. It dims the Prompt card and prints the note under
          it, so the box stops looking like the dial it is not; dead_on_fast also disables it
          while fast is selected. Only claim this from a measurement: WanMove earned it over
          four renders on one seed and field.
seed    [node, input] the seed goes on (optional)
node    the model node that carries size, length and the reference slots
size    megapixels + multiple the width/height are fitted to, and the input names
length  frame count: the model's fps, its frame-count step (snap) and floor, and the lengths to
offer on the panel. A model that takes seconds instead can set "unit": "seconds".
refs    the auto-growing picture slots: a {i} template, the prefix to clear first, and how many

video   the clip slots: {"slot": "ref_videos.ref_video_{i}", "clear": prefix to wipe first,
          "audio": the matching audio slot, "audio_clear": its prefix, "max": how many}.
          A slot name with no {i} is the old single-clip shape and still works. H3 reads up
          to three videos at once and the prompt names them <Video 1..3>, which is what a
          colour mask steering several contexts needs.
tracks  {"coords": [node, input]} for a motion-control graph: DWARP measures a video's
movement (engine/tracks.py) and writes the path JSON straight onto that input. The
Motion slot on the panel appears only for a workflow that has this key.
sound   whether the file it writes has audio at all
extra   {"saver": node, "name": "label"} for a second output the graph writes — WanMove's track visualiser, say. It lands in the run's post folder and shows as a chip under the stage.
strength {"input": name, "min", "max", "step", "default"} — one number on the model node, shown as a slider. WanMove uses it for how hard the tracks pull the picture.

speed   {"node", "input", "fast": value, "note", "fast_note"} — one boolean in the graph that swaps a whole recipe at once (WanMove's switch feeds model, steps and CFG together). It puts the quality / fast pair on the panel; the notes are its tooltips.

brief   true when the model reads a sectioned brief rather than a line of description. It is what puts the "Start from" template picker and the tall monospace prompt box on the panel; a model with an ordinary text encoder leaves it out and gets the usual prompt box.
Leave a key out and that control disappears from the panel.

kind    "render" (the default) builds a clip and belongs in the panel's Workflow dropdown.
          "upscale" takes a finished run's mp4 and hands back a bigger one; those appear in
          Enhance instead, under Upscale -> cloud, and never in the panel.
  input   [node, input] the mp4 goes on, for an upscale graph (its LoadVideo file widget).
  controls what the Enhance panel shows for an upscale graph, in order. One entry per knob:
          {"id", "label", "kind": number | choice | toggle, "node", "input", "default", "note"}
          plus "min"/"max"/"step" for a number and "options" for a choice. The page builds the
          controls from this list, so picking a different upscaler changes the controls with it
          and adding one is still a JSON entry.
  cost    one line saying how this graph bills — shown under the picker, because Enhance is
          otherwise entirely local and a cloud entry is the first button there that spends.

A graph that wraps its work in a subgraph (node types that look like a UUID) cannot be written by
hand: /api/prompt takes a flat graph. Open it in the Comfy editor and use Workflow -> Export (API),
which flattens the subgraphs, then drop the file in here and name it in an entry.

A graph may run a real model on a cloud GPU, or call out to a partner through an API node
(api_node: true in the catalogue). Both go through the same submit, and the key rides in extra_data as
well as the header so the API nodes are authorised too - without it a partner node answers
"Unauthorized: Please login first to use this node". They bill differently, which is what `cost` is for.

workflows.label: H3 · Pika Flex
workflows.note: Reference to video, with sound. Up to nine pictures and your clip go in; a new 5-15 s clip comes out, picture and audio made together. Six sampling steps, native 1344x768.

workflows.label: H3 · Context Smash
workflows.note: Several whole videos in H3’s context at once, named in the prompt. Up to three videos and nine pictures go in; what comes out borrows from all of them. The trick is to make one of the videos a flat colour mask and tell the prompt which colour means which video — that is what decides where each context lands and when. 5-15 s, with sound.

workflows.label: WanMove · motion control
workflows.note: Image to video along paths. One picture plus measured motion: the picture stays, and whatever the tracks do is what moves. Drop a clip (or one of your renders) into Motion to measure them. No sound. 16 fps, 480p-class.

prompt_hint.note: Barely read here: the motion comes from the paths, not the words. Measured over four renders on one seed and field — a completely different scene prompt moved colour a little and changed nothing else, and on fast it did nothing at all.

speed.note: 20 steps at CFG 6, the full model
speed.fast_note: 6 steps at CFG 1 with the lightx2v step-distill LoRA — roughly 3x quicker, a little softer

workflows.label: FlashVSR · fast
workflows.note: One pass to a fixed height. Sharpens and de-artifacts without repainting, and holds still between frames.
workflows.cost: Runs as a partner API node — billed per call, not against GPU time.

controls.label: Target
controls.note: The height it upscales to, whatever came in.

workflows.label: Clarity Crystal · faithful
workflows.note: Multiplies the frame size and stays close to what it was given — it restores rather than invents. Keeps the frame count and the sound.
workflows.cost: Runs as a partner API node — billed per call, not against GPU time. Over 30 fps costs 2x, over 60 fps 3x.
workflows.limits: Capped at 9 megapixels a frame and 360 megapixel-seconds a clip, so a long or large clip comes back upscaled by less than you asked for.

controls.label: Scale
controls.note: Multiplies width and height: 2 doubles both.

workflows.label: Wan 2.2 Creative
workflows.model: Wan 2.2 T2V A14B fp8 + lightx2v step-distill LoRA · 4 steps, CFG 1, euler
workflows.note: A diffusion pass rather than a resample: it repaints as it enlarges, so it invents detail that was never there. Closest in spirit to Refine, but on their card.
workflows.cost: A GPU workflow — it runs the real model on a Comfy Cloud GPU and bills GPU time, not per call like the partner upscalers.

controls.label: Scale
controls.note: Multiplies the run's own frame size, so the shape it was rendered in is kept.

controls.label: Creative
controls.note: How much it is allowed to repaint. Low adds texture, high changes what is there.

controls.label: Prompt
controls.note: What the new detail should look like.
